issues.passage: The notional duty of the editor was to fact-check every claim before publication.
issues.why: "Notional duty" is natural, correct English for a duty that exists only in theory or on paper (notional = hypothetical/theoretical). A student who knows the definition would rightly accept this passage.

fix.correctPassage: The budget included only a notional amount for travel until actual costs were known.
wrongPassages: The notional figures were wire-transferred and already spent by Tuesday.
City officials granted a notional license that authorized the restaurant to open at once.
Negotiators filed the notional draft as a signed, fully enforceable contract.

issues.passage: She chose to impart nothing and sealed the research notes from every colleague.
issues.why: "Impart nothing" is correct usage: to make no information known / share nothing. Choosing not to impart is still a valid use of the verb, not a misuse.

fix.correctPassage: Good mentors impart not only techniques but also habits of careful reading.
wrongPassages: Editors carefully impart spoilers from the review copy so early readers stay surprised.
The filter is designed to impart impurities from the sample before analysis.
Inspectors tried to impart a confession from the reluctant witness.
